title: [R3-5 follow-up] Durable policy decision for graph.supersede: evaluate the supersession subject and bind policyDecisionRef to its digest
description:
FILED BY R3-5 PLANNING (task-b54b560991704162aed1f71814596cac, measured 2026-08-28 at the tree after 23682c14). GAP, symbol by symbol: no production writer records a policy decision for a SUPERSESSION subject and no daemon reader yields one. `grep -rn policyDecisionRef apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test` returns only demo-seed-payloads.ts:405 (null), policy-risk-leg.ts:63/79 (bdbe0519 activation-path WIP, records the caller's ref, verifies it against nothing) and recovery-completion.ts (applicablePolicyRef only). PolicyEvaluated readers (activation/policy-admission-reader.ts readPolicyAdmission, bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts readPolicyEvaluationAuthority) key on action "effect.activate" + one node subject; the bootstrap journey's own row is action "plan.approve" with scope [] (bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:241-251). Nothing evaluates policy for action graph.supersede over the successor revision.

R3-5 therefore binds `policyDecisionRef` to the daemon's DURABLE ABSENCE of a supersession decision: null matches, any non-null ref refuses GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_APPROVAL_POLICY_DECISION_MISMATCH (fail-closed, never verified against an unrelated row). This row replaces that absence with a real fact.

SCOPE: (1) a production writer that evaluates the installed policy slice for the supersession subject (action graph.supersede, graphNodeRevisionRefs [successorRevisionRef], scope = successor node keys) through the existing policy.validate/evaluatePolicy path, sealed as PolicyEvaluated with decisionDigest; (2) a daemon reader `readSupersessionPolicyDecision(store, projectId, successorRevisionRef)` beside policy-admission-reader.ts, verifying via readPolicyEvaluationAuthority and refusing legacy/foreign rows; (3) flip the matcher in apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts from null-equality to digest equality, update successorBoundApprovalRecord(store) in graph-supersede-test-fixtures.ts to derive the digest through the reader, keep the seven hostile arms green and add the null-now-refuses arm; (4) also bind applicablePolicyRef to the same row's policyRef if it disagrees with the inherited boundHashes.policyHash — measure first.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK on disk: R3-5's matcher exists at apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts and compares policyDecisionRef against null (grep -n policyDecisionRef); no production writer yet seals a PolicyEvaluated row with action graph.supersede (grep -rn '"graph.supersede"' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap apps/daemon/src/planning | grep -v test) — else adopt or block as duplicate.

A production writer seals a PolicyEvaluated row for the supersession subject through the existing evaluatePolicy/decisionDigestFor path, exercised by a test that drives the PRODUCTION command surface (no fixture-authored row).

A daemon reader returns that row's decisionDigest for (projectId, successorRevisionRef) and refuses with a stable code on absence, legacy shape, foreign subject, or later install reuse — asserted by code AND layer per arm.

The graph.supersede matcher compares record.policyDecisionRef to the reader's digest; the accepted control derives its record through the reader; a null policyDecisionRef now refuses GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_APPROVAL_POLICY_DECISION_MISMATCH; the drop-comparison drill reds exactly that arm.

Gates standalone: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck ($ tsc echo) and the focused daemon vitest run over the supersede suites with nonzero counts; every production file <=400 lines; explicit-pathspec commit.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 3 — THE WRITER AND THE READER. New modules under `apps/daemon/src/planning/`, each <=250 lines, EACH WITH ITS `.js` BRIDGE — this tree uses bridges beside every `.ts`; a missing one is invisible to tsc and vitest and reds unrelated files at runtime.

(A) THE WRITER seals a PolicyEvaluated row for the SUPERSESSION SUBJECT through the existing evaluate/`decisionDigestFor` path (bootstrap-policy-authority.ts:108). DoD-2 requires it be exercised by a test driving the PRODUCTION command surface — no fixture-authored row. Compose the digest authority; do NOT hash locally, and do NOT introduce a second `decisionDigest` notion. The subject must identify the supersession unambiguously: at minimum the project and the successor revision, so a row sealed for one supersession cannot answer for another.

(B) THE READER returns that row's `decisionDigest` for `(projectId, successorRevisionRef)`. Build on the GENERIC seam `bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts`, which carries `action` as a field (:36, :182, :208) rather than pinning one — NOT on `activation/policy-admission-reader.ts`, which hard-refuses anything but `effect.activate` at :74 and is the wrong scope.
DoD-3 names FOUR refusal arms and each asserts an EXACT stable code AND the refusing layer, never merely that it failed: ABSENCE (no row for the subject), LEGACY SHAPE (a row missing the fields this reader needs), FOREIGN SUBJECT (a row sealed for a different project or successor — this is the arm that stops one supersession's decision authorising another), and LATER INSTALL REUSE (a row from a superseded policy install answering for the current one).

BEFORE CHOOSING ANY REFUSAL CODE, grep the runtime error registry for which codes admit the aggregate this reader uses. `createRuntimeError` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-factory.ts:93-104) returns `UNKNOWN_ERROR` and DOES NOT THROW when the code is unknown or the descriptor does not list the aggregate — so a wrong code compiles, runs, refuses, and silently loses its identity while every "it refused" arm stays green. `sourceAccepted` (:79-86) checks the aggregate ONLY, never the descriptor's `cmds(...)` list. Add a dedicated arm asserting NO refusal this reader produces has code `UNKNOWN_ERROR`, and drill it in step 5.

Re-run step 2's command: arms (1) and (2) go green; arm (3) stays red — the matcher flip is step 4 and it is correct for it to still be inverted here.

STEP 4 — FLIP THE MATCHER AND CARRY THE FAN-OUT IN THE SAME COMMIT.

(A) THE FLIP, at `graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts:89-92`. Replace the absence-passes branch with a comparison of `record.policyDecisionRef` against the digest step 3's READER returns for this supersession. Delete the `// task-9fb4e53d... will replace absence with a durable digest.` comment — it is now discharged, and a stale marker naming a completed row misroutes the next reader.
AFTER THIS: a null `policyDecisionRef` REFUSES `GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_APPROVAL_POLICY_DECISION_MISMATCH` (DoD-4), a matching digest passes, and a non-matching one refuses with the same code. Keep the code and the module-private layer unchanged — the row adds authority, it does not add vocabulary.

(B) THE FAN-OUT, and it must land in THIS commit or the branch goes red for everyone. Every consumer enumerated in step 2 moves now:
- `graph-supersede-test-fixtures.ts`'s successor-bound record builder must DERIVE its `policyDecisionRef` from the reader rather than setting null. DO NOT import the matcher module into the fixture to compute the expected value — an expected value taken from the module under test is a FIXED POINT that step 5's drill could never red. Derive it from the READER, or from the durable row the writer sealed.
- The accepted controls in `graph-supersede-approval-binding.test.ts` now derive a real digest and still DECIDE.
- Any supersede arm elsewhere that passes a literal null is updated, or explicitly re-purposed into a refusal arm asserting the new code and layer.

(C) DoD-4's ACCEPTED CONTROL derives its record THROUGH THE READER — that is what makes it a production-surface proof rather than a fixture agreeing with itself.

Re-run step 2's command plus the supersede service and refusals suites: all green, both count lines quoted.

STEP 5 — DRILLS, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE HANDOFF.

RESTORE PROTOCOL: the three tracked files were porcelain-CLEAN at plan time, so `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` IS a valid restore proof for them — but re-check `git status --porcelain` per path first, because they will carry YOUR edits during the drills. The new modules are UNTRACKED until commit and `git diff` is BLIND to them, so back those to `%TEMP%/9fb4e53d-<workerId>/` and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (64 hex, non-empty, equal). Confirm each mutation LANDED before rerunning; a silent no-op write reads as green.
D1 THE COMPARISON IS LOAD-BEARING (DoD-4's named drill): drop the policyDecisionRef comparison entirely -> the null-refuses arm MUST red. If it stays green the flip is decorative.
D2 ABSENCE IS NOT A PASS: make the reader return a digest when no row exists -> the reader's ABSENCE arm reds, and ONLY it. This is the arm that stops the row silently restoring the behaviour it was filed to remove.
D3 FOREIGN SUBJECT: have the reader ignore the successor revision when selecting the row -> the foreign-subject arm reds. That arm is what stops one supersession's policy decision authorising another, so it must fail for that reason and not on a shape check.
D4 SILENT DEGRADATION: change one refusal's `source.aggregate` to a value the descriptor does not list -> the anti-UNKNOWN_ERROR arm MUST red. The mutant compiles, runs and still refuses, which is exactly why that arm exists.
D5 NOT A FIXED POINT: change the writer's sealed material so the digest differs -> the accepted control MUST red. If it stays green, the fixture derived its expectation from the module under test rather than from the reader.
A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in the row comment, never a pass to bank.

GATES — each alone, FOREGROUND, UNPIPED. An exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING and is UNVERIFIED.
LEG A: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — exit 0, quote the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo. Sub-second? plant one type error as a positive control, confirm red, remove, prove by SHA256 in a separate call.
LEG B: `(cd apps/daemon && pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/planning/graph-supersede-approval-binding.test.ts src/planning/supersession-policy-decision.test.ts src/planning/graph-supersede-service.test.ts src/planning/graph-supersede-refusals.test.ts)` — exit 0, quote BOTH count lines. The service and refusals suites are included deliberately: they are where a missed null-passing arm will surface.
LEG C: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` for attribution — the failing-path set at HEAD minus merge-base, intersected with this row's owned paths, must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red VERBATIM with exact failing lines and paths; never edit it, never block on it.
CLEAN-CHECKOUT PROOF: after committing, `git grep -n "policyDecisionRef" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts` must show the comparison and NOT the old null-passes branch, and the discharged `task-9fb4e53d` marker comment must be GONE from HEAD.
LINE CAPS: `wc -l` every production file; each <=250 target, under 400 hard.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, in the step note: can a supersession still decide with a null policyDecisionRef by any route; can a row sealed for one project or successor answer for another (D3 is the guard); is the digest derived once through `decisionDigestFor` with no second derivation anywhere; did any expectation end up copied from the module under test; does every new `.ts` have its `.js` bridge; and can any refusal produce `UNKNOWN_ERROR`.

DURABLE HANDOFF — moe.add_comment, not the completion summary. Keep each under ~4500 chars and SPLIT rather than truncate (both surfaces cap at 5000 SILENTLY). Carry step 1's gate measurements WITH the freshly-captured HEAD sha beside each grep — INCLUDING the correction that `policy-evaluation.ts` is not in HEAD, so the next reader does not chase it — the step-2 fan-out roster with file and line for every policyDecisionRef consumer, the five drill outcomes with restore proofs, Leg A/B/C exit codes and count lines, and the clean-checkout greps. Name task-b54b5609 (R3-5) as the row whose matcher line this discharges. Commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC of this row's owned paths, message BEFORE the `--` (a `-m` after `--` is parsed as a pathspec and nothing lands). Never `git add -A`, never a bare `git commit` — the index is shared and carries foreign entries.
